title: Dirac–Motzkin below the Green–Tao threshold
premise_risks: Green–Tao's n₀ may have been made explicit somewhere (thesis or follow-up); not found
Famous conjecture's residual range; the weaker target is the realistic extended-set ask
plain: Given n points in the plane, not all on one line, an ordinary line is a line through exactly two of them. Green and Tao proved that for all sufficiently large n there are at least n/2 ordinary lines, but they never made 'sufficiently large' explicit. The best bound proved for every n is 6n/13. Prove n/2 for every n except the two known exceptions, 7 and 13, or at least beat 6n/13 for all n ≥ 14.
math: For finite non-collinear $P\subset\mathbb R^2$ with $|P|=n$, let $t_2(P)$ be the number of lines meeting $P$ in exactly two points. Prove $t_2(P)\ge n/2$ for all $n\notin\{7,13\}$. By Green–Tao this is known for $n\ge n_0$, so the content is the finite range $n<n_0$ (or making $n_0$ explicit and verifying below it). Weaker target: find $c>6/13$ with $t_2(P)\ge cn$ for all $n\ge 14$.
review_note: Known: $t_2\ge 3n/7$: Kelly–Moser (1958). $t_2\ge 6n/13$ for $n\ne 7$: Csima–Sawyer, DCG 9 (1993). For $n\ge n_0$: $t_2\ge n/2$ for even $n$ and $t_2\ge 3\lfloor n/4\rfloor$ for odd $n$, both sharp (Green–Tao, DCG 50 (2013), arXiv:1208.4714). Exceptions: $n=7$ ($t_2=3$, Kelly–Moser) and $n=13$ ($t_2=6$, Crowe–McKee). Recent related work, which does not improve this: arXiv:2610.21415 (2026, ordinary lines in $\mathbb C^3$) and Dumitrescu–Pach, EJC 33(3) P3.33 (2026).
